questions.question: What defines discontinuous variation in living organisms?
options: Features that can take any numerical value within a range.
Features that have limited variations falling into distinct, separate categories.
Features that only change as an organism grows older.
Features that are determined entirely by the climate they live in.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes continuous variation?
options: Features that can only be classified into yes or no answers.
Features that can take any value within a range.
Features that are passed down only from the maternal parent.
Features that do not change from generation to generation.

questions.question: Which of these features in humans represents discontinuous variation?
Which type of graph is most appropriate for displaying continuous data, such as the heights of a group of students?
What factors usually influence continuous variation in organisms?
options: Only the temperature of the surroundings.
Purely genetic factors with no environmental influence.
Only the diet of the organism during early development.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate way to display discontinuous data, such as eye colour or blood group?
What is the primary cause of discontinuous variation in organisms?
options: It is usually caused only by genetics and is not affected by environment or lifestyle.
It is determined purely by the nutrient intake of the organism.
It is shaped entirely by physical exercise and lifestyle choices.
It is caused by accidental injuries sustained during an organism's life.

questions.question: When organisms reproduce, what is the term for them producing offspring of the same kind?
Why do offspring tend to look similar to their parents and to each other (family resemblance)?
options: Because they inherit features from both parents.
Because they live in the exact same environment.
Because they copy the behaviors of their siblings.
Because they have identical environmental exposure.

questions.question: How are inherited features passed from parents to offspring during reproduction?
options: Through the transfer of nutrients in food.
Through DNA passed from parents to offspring.
Through the copy of learned physical skills.
Through environmental exposure in the womb.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature that is primarily caused or changed by an organism's lifestyle and environment?
Which statement is true regarding variation between offspring?
options: Offspring are always genetically identical to their parents.
There is usually variation between offspring; they are not usually identical to their parents or each other.
Offspring only show variation if they are raised in different countries.
Offspring of the same parents have no physical differences.

questions.question: How do differences between species compare to differences within species?
options: Differences between species are smaller than differences within species.
Differences between species are greater than differences within species.
There are no differences between species.
Differences within species are always identical to differences between species.
